problem.text: A positive integer $N$ has base-eleven representation $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}$ and base-eight representation $\underline{1}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}\,\underline{a}$, where $a, b,$ and $c$ represent (not necessarily distinct) digits. Find the least such $N$ expressed in base ten.

steps.title: Where to start: turn both representations into base ten
steps.body: Both digit strings name the same number $N$. If we write each one out using place values, we get two expressions for $N$ that must be equal, which gives an equation in $a$, $b$ and $c$.

your_turn.prompt: Write $\underline{a}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}$ in base eleven and $\underline{1}\,\underline{b}\,\underline{c}\,\underline{a}$ in base eight as base-ten expressions.

steps.title: Set them equal and simplify
steps.body:
Setting the two expressions equal and moving like terms together gives one clean equation.
$$120a = 512 + 53b + 7c$$
The digits also have limits. The same $a$, $b$, $c$ appear in a base-eight number, so each must be a base-eight digit.

your_turn.answer: $0$ through $7$. Base eleven would allow up to $10$, but base eight only allows digits up to $7$.

steps.title: Find the smallest possible $a$
steps.body: The right side is at least $512$, so $120a$ must be at least $512$. To make $N = 121a + 11b + c$ as small as possible we want the smallest $a$ that works, because $11b + c \le 84$ is always less than $121$, so a smaller $a$ always wins.

your_turn.prompt: Why can $a$ not be $4$? What is the smallest $a$ to try?
your_turn.answer: $120\cdot 4 = 480$, which is less than $512$. So try $a = 5$.

steps.title: Solve for $b$ and $c$
steps.body: With $a = 5$ the left side is $600$, so the equation becomes $53b + 7c = 88$. Now $b$ and $c$ must be digits from $0$ to $7$, so only a few values of $b$ are possible.

your_turn.prompt: Try $b = 0$ and $b = 1$. Which one gives a digit $c$?
your_turn.answer: $b = 0$ needs $7c = 88$, not a whole number. $b = 1$ gives $7c = 35$, so $c = 5$. ($b = 2$ is already too big: $106 > 88$.)

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The digits are $a = 5$, $b = 1$, $c = 5$. In base eleven, $N = 121\cdot 5 + 11\cdot 1 + 5 = 621$. Check with base eight: $1155_8 = 512 + 64 + 40 + 5 = 621$. The least such $N$ is $621$.
